position: CFTC Administration and Improved Commodities and Derivatives Markets
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the CFTC replace its existing position limits rule, which the chapter says reduces liquidity and raises volatility, with further delegation to exchanges to set position limits and accountability levels where appropriate. It also recommends reducing overly prescriptive rules that implement the CFTC's core principles.
remaining: Replacing the Part 150 position limits with exchange-set limits

sources.title: Order Sunsetting Certain Large Trader Reporting Requirements for Physical Commodity Swaps
Swap Execution Facility Order Book Requirement for Permitted Transactions

status_summary: No CFTC proposal or order replacing the federal position limits rule with exchange delegation was found; a final order published 2026-07-21 (91 FR 45638) sunsets routine large trader reporting for physical commodity swaps and leaves the Part 150 position limits in place. On core principle rules, CFTC staff gave no-action relief on 2025-07-30 (letter 25-24) from the SEF order book requirement for swaps not subject to the trade execution requirement, and the Commission proposed on 2026-08-26 (91 FR 55030, comments closed 2026-09-25) to codify that change; the order book requirement comes from the 2013 SEF core principles rule.

timeline.event: CFTC staff issued no-action letter 25-24 giving relief from the SEF order book requirement for permitted transactions (as described in the 2026-08-26 proposal).
The CFTC published a proposed rule (91 FR 55030) to remove the SEF order book requirement for permitted transactions; comments closed 2026-09-25.

title: Replace CFTC position limits with exchange delegation; trim core principle rules

Whether the SEF proposal counts as trimming core principle rules is a judgment call.
